Schoolgirl, author and seasoned mudlark Emmylou Vaxby has spent nearly a decade searching the Thames foreshore for fragments of the city’s past. Fleur Britten joins her at low tide to see what turns up

It’s a mild Sunday morning in late September, and I’m on the north bank of the Thames near Wapping. It’s surprisingly tranquil down here – the din of the city has been replaced with the sound of gently lapping waves; the bustling crowds with an occasional dog walker. I’m with 14-year-old Emmylou Vaxby, a London schoolgirl, mudlark – a forager of artefacts on a riverbank – and author of A Guide to Mudlarking on the River Thames. We are here, of course, to mudlark.

Actual Article Body:
Authorities are trying to determine what prompted an apparent stranger to allegedly stab to death a seven-year-old girl on a Chicago sidewalk on Saturday.

The alleged assailant, reportedly a 48-year-old woman whose name so far has not been released by police, was chased down by bystanders after she stabbed the little girl in back multiple times, the Chicago NBC affiliate Channel 5 reported.

The victim has been identified by the Cook County Medical Examiner as Edi Mari Hernandez Chacon, who was pronounced dead at a local hospital after the attack.
